title: Ontellus Reviews 2026
summary: Ontellus reviews, covering the company, its SmartTools suite, records retrieval services, integrations, pricing, and the Datavant acquisition, plus how Codes Health adds plaintiff-focused AI analysis on a flat fee.
body_markdown:
Ontellus turns up on most shortlists when firms compare records retrieval vendors, and it has the scale to justify that. What's less obvious from the outside is what the company actually sells, who it built those products for, and what changed when Datavant acquired it. This review covers the company, its service lines and SmartTools suite, pricing and turnaround, and how it compares to a platform like[the Codes Health workflow](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) built specifically around plaintiff litigation workflows.


## **Key Takeaways**


-


Ontellus traces its roots to 1975 and operates from Houston, rebranding from Keais Records Retrieval in May 2017 after seven acquisitions consolidated it into a nationwide retrieval provider


-


Datavant completed its acquisition of Ontellus on August 6, 2025, forming a Legal and Insurance vertical led by former Ontellus CEO Vince Cole


-


The company serves insurance carriers, self-insured corporations, law firms, custodians, and clinical life sciences, with published segments spanning workers compensation, general liability, medical malpractice, mass tort and MDL


-


Its SmartTools suite covers chronology, indexing, and secure distribution, with SmartChron priced at a flat rate per file


-


Ontellus's public materials do not advertise AI litigation analysis such as breach-in-care identification or documented future expense extraction


-


Codes Health works toward complete records in a couple of weeks with retrieval, AI analysis, and human verification in one flat-fee workflow


-


Incomplete authorizations are a leading cause of denied requests, and pre-submission AI validation catches them before a resubmission is needed


## **Ontellus: Company Overview**


Ontellus operates from Houston, Texas, and traces its origins to 1975. The company most people know today took shape in May 2017, when Keais Records Retrieval rebranded as Ontellus after completing seven acquisitions, including Second Image National, Legal Partners, RSP & Associates, Quest Discovery Services, and National Document Services. At the time of the rebrand it reported more than 500 employees nationwide and described itself as the largest pure-play nationwide data retrieval provider serving the insurance and legal claims industry.


That consolidation history explains a lot about the company's current shape. Ontellus is less a single product than an assembled group of retrieval operations, investigative services, and document tools brought under one brand.


In 2025, the company changed hands again. Datavant completed its acquisition of Ontellus on August 6, 2025, and established a Legal and Insurance business vertical led by former Ontellus CEO Vince Cole. Datavant operates a health data network spanning more than 80,000 hospitals and clinics.


### **Who Ontellus Serves**


The published customer segments run wider than retrieval alone:


-


Insurance carriers and self-insured corporations


-


Law firms, including mass tort and MDL practices


-


Workers’ compensation, general liability, and vehicle and bodily injury claims


-


Medical malpractice and life insurance


-


Record custodians and clinical life sciences organizations


-


Special investigations units


Worth noting for plaintiff firms evaluating the company: legal is a genuine published segment here, not an afterthought. The design center still leans toward claims and carrier workflows, but Ontellus does market directly to law firms.


## **What Ontellus Retrieves**


The retrieval catalog is broad and goes well past clinical charts:


-


Medical and billing records


-


Wage and employment records


-


Diagnostic imaging files


-


Pharmacy records


-


Social Security records


-


Foreign subpoenas and subpoena-driven workflows


For firms handling workers' compensation or claims-heavy matters where wage and employment documentation carries as much weight as treatment records, that breadth is a real differentiator against retrieval vendors focused only on medical charts.


## **The SmartTools Suite**


Ontellus's proprietary tools sit inside the My.Ontellus portal, which handles request submission, tracking, and Secure Records Delivery.


**SmartChron** aggregates case records into a single chronological file organized by date, provider, and record type, letting reviewers identify providers and medical events quickly and jump to relevant pages in one click. Ontellus says records processed through its charting tool are ready for review within 24 to 48 hours. It's billed at a flat rate per file, which the company positions against hourly billing for records preparation.


**SmartOrg** lets teams upload records they already hold so those get processed the same way as newly retrieved ones. Everything gets organized, Bates labeled, and run through OCR, producing a searchable file with a hyperlinked table of contents. Ontellus says existing records are ready for review in under 24 hours, and that SmartOrg output can feed into a SmartChron file.


**SmartShare** distributes records alongside other documents and reports back on viewing activity, which gives some visibility into where protected health information has traveled.


**SmartPricing** appears in the company's legal materials as part of the SmartTools set.


## **Additional Services**


Beyond retrieval and organization, Ontellus and its affiliated businesses offer:


-


**Medical canvassing** through INTERTEL, for locating treatment facilities a claimant didn't disclose


-


**Social media investigation** and Social e-Profiler


-


**DICOM viewer** for diagnostic imaging


-


**Claim evaluation reports** and billing summaries


-


**Expert witness access** through AMFS, which reports more than 6,000 expert witnesses across 212 medical specialties


-


**ChartSwap** , a business-to-business record exchange connecting requestors and providers


Medical canvassing is the piece plaintiff firms tend to care about most, since undisclosed providers are a common source of incomplete record sets.


## **Integrations**


Ontellus publishes integrations with Guidewire and a partnership with Duck Creek, both of which are insurance claims platforms rather than legal case management systems. It also references third-party integrations more generally.


Firms running Filevine, Litify, or similar case management software should confirm what connectivity exists before assuming a fit, since the named integrations point squarely at the carrier side of the market.


## **Turnaround and Pricing**


Ontellus markets industry-leading turnaround times without publishing a single headline retrieval figure across the pages reviewed here. SmartChron and SmartOrg carry specific processing commitments, 24 to 48 hours and under 24 hours respectively, but those describe how fast obtained records get organized rather than how long retrieval itself takes. Ask for the retrieval number directly.


Pricing is not published. The company operates on transaction-based fees with pricing set per retrieval or bundled for volume, so expect a custom quote. SmartChron is the exception, billed at a flat rate per file.


## **Data Security**


Ontellus maintains a dedicated data security function and states that it holds SOC 2 Type II certification with recurring audits of relevant controls. Several other retrieval vendors report the same certification. Records move through the HIPAA-compliant My.Ontellus portal.


As with any vendor handling protected health information, confirm business associate agreement terms, retention policies, and incident response procedures directly.


## **Customer Feedback and Market Presence**


Ontellus publishes customer testimonials on its own site, with recurring themes around persistent provider follow-up, staff professionalism, and the convenience of entering case information once and adding subpoena locations without re-keying.


Public review platforms tell a more mixed story. Consumer review sites show notably lower ratings than the company's own testimonials suggest, with comments touching on record organization, while workplace review sites show middling employee sentiment alongside stronger culture scores elsewhere. Discussion forums include paralegals describing long timelines on individual matters, duplicate records, and facilities that weren't identified.


Ratings and review counts shift constantly, so check current listings directly rather than relying on a number quoted in any article. Individual experiences also may not represent typical outcomes. The more useful step is asking for references from firms with similar practice areas and caseloads.


## **Where Ontellus Stops and Litigation AI Begins**


Here's the honest line. Ontellus has genuine records organization technology. SmartChron produces a real chronology, SmartOrg handles OCR and indexing properly, and the canvassing and imaging services close gaps that many retrieval vendors leave open.


What the public materials do not advertise is AI analysis built around plaintiff case theory: breach-in-care identification, documented future medical expense extraction, pre-existing condition flagging tied to litigation strategy, or proactive AI missing record detection that cross-references a patient's history before delivery. Organizing records chronologically and analyzing them for case-relevant findings are different jobs.


### **What Integrated Litigation Analysis Adds**


[The Codes Health platform](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) combines retrieval with analysis in one workflow:


-


**AI-powered case chronologies** grouping encounters and bills by visit, exposing treatment gaps, and preserving links back to source documents


-


**Breach-in-care identification** for medical malpractice work


-


**Documented future medical expenses** extracted for damages support


-


**Pre-existing condition flagging** and other hidden case facts


-


**Proactive missing record detection** cross-referencing patient history to find gaps before delivery


-


**Authorization validation** catching misspellings, missing signatures, unclear expiration dates, and missing dates of service before submission


All of it passes through human verification before delivery, which Codes Health describes as AI insights verified by humans. It works toward complete records in a couple of weeks on a flat fee.


Worth separating this from general-purpose tools some firms try first. General AI platforms like ChatGPT are not designed for litigation-grade medical record review. They don't retrieve records, validate authorizations, follow up with providers, or verify completeness. Codes Health's platform is built for this work and analyzes records with high precision for legal teams.


On speed claims across the market, Codes Health notes that services advertising same-day retrieval typically return only what's already available electronically, leaving the firm or client to chase the rest, an experience it says contributes to churn. Codes Health does not market same-day delivery.


Its MIT-educated engineering team keeps building out additional workflows and products, so the platform continues to evolve, improve, and grow more comprehensive as the demands of modern legal practices change. For high-volume customers, it also builds custom integrations with CRM platforms and other medical software, alongside its embedded[Filevine partnership workflow](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/blogs/best-ontellus-alternatives-for-legal-medical-record-retrieval) .


## **Choosing the Right Retrieval Partner for Your Practice**


**Choose Ontellus when:**


-


Your matters need wage, employment, pharmacy, or Social Security records alongside medical charts


-


Medical canvassing for undisclosed providers is a recurring need


-


You run claims-side work where Guidewire or Duck Creek integration matters


-


Expert witness sourcing or foreign subpoena handling would otherwise mean another vendor


-


Chronological organization of records you already hold is the main gap


**Choose Codes Health when:**


-


You want retrieval and[litigation analysis together](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/blogs/best-ontellus-alternatives-for-legal-medical-record-retrieval) rather than organization alone


-


Breach-in-care insights and documented future expense extraction matter to your cases


-


Proactive missing record detection before trial is a priority


-


Human verification of AI insights before delivery is a requirement


-


Flat-fee predictability beats a custom quote per engagement


-


An embedded Filevine workflow or custom CRM build fits your stack


### **Questions to Ask Any Vendor**


Ask for the actual retrieval turnaround rather than the document processing time, how the vendor handles providers who don't respond, what the AI does and where it sits in the workflow, how completeness is verified before delivery, what the full fee structure looks like including provider costs, which case management integrations exist beyond claims platforms, and whether you can speak with references from firms with similar practice areas.


## **The Bottom Line**


Ontellus is a company built by acquisition, and that shows in the catalog. Wage records, pharmacy records, imaging, canvassing, expert witnesses, foreign subpoenas, social investigation: very few vendors cover that much ground. If your matters pull documents from all over, that breadth is genuinely hard to replicate elsewhere.


The design center is still claims. The named integrations are carrier platforms. The tooling organizes records well but stops short of reading them for case theory. And with the Datavant acquisition now folded into a Legal and Insurance vertical, it's fair to ask what the roadmap prioritizes over the next few years.


For a plaintiff firm, the question is what you need done to the records once they arrive. Chronological order and OCR are useful. Knowing which entries suggest a breach in care, which documented expenses support your damages number, and which facility never showed up at all is a different deliverable.[Codes Health was built](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) for that second job, with retrieval attached to it rather than sold separately. Run one matter through both and the difference in what lands on your desk will be obvious.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **What does Ontellus retrieve besides medical records?**


Ontellus retrieves billing records, wage and employment records, diagnostic imaging files, pharmacy records, and social security records, and handles foreign subpoenas. It also offers medical canvassing through INTERTEL for locating undisclosed treatment facilities, social media investigation, a DICOM viewer, billing summaries, and claim evaluation reports.


### **What are SmartChron and SmartOrg?**


SmartChron aggregates case records into a single chronological file organized by date, provider, and record type, with records ready for review within 24 to 48 hours and billing at a flat rate per file. SmartOrg processes records a firm already holds, applying organization, Bates labeling, and OCR to produce a searchable file with a hyperlinked table of contents, ready in under 24 hours.


### **How did the Datavant acquisition change Ontellus?**


Datavant completed the acquisition on August 6, 2025 and created a Legal and Insurance business vertical led by former Ontellus CEO Vince Cole. Datavant's health data network spans more than 80,000 hospitals and clinics, which may broaden digital retrieval reach. Ask about roadmap and contract terms directly, since integration details have not been fully detailed publicly.


### **Does Ontellus analyze records for litigation?**


Ontellus organizes records chronologically through SmartChron and indexes them through SmartOrg. Its public materials do not advertise AI analysis built around plaintiff case theory such as breach-in-care identification or documented future expense extraction.[Codes Health delivers those](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/blogs/llamalab-vs-digitalowl-vs-codes-health) as part of the same workflow as retrieval, with human verification before delivery.


### **What does Ontellus cost?**


Ontellus does not publish pricing. It operates on transaction-based fees, with costs set per retrieval or bundled for volume, so most engagements require a custom quote. SmartChron is billed at a flat rate per file. Codes Health uses flat-fee pricing across retrieval and AI analysis together.


### **Does Ontellus integrate with legal case management software?**


Ontellus publishes integrations with Guidewire and a partnership with Duck Creek, which are insurance claims platforms, and references third-party integrations more broadly. Firms running legal case management software should confirm available connectivity directly. Codes Health has an embedded Filevine workflow and builds custom CRM integrations for high-volume customers.
